The panel exists now - [data-testid=barn-open-raw-output] reads 'Show raw output · vue-cli-service serve · the terminal is still here' and opening it sets aria-expanded=true - but it never shows a line. It reported 'the dev server's log could not be read: HTTP 406' and the foot read 'The last 0 of them.' The cause is one header: devServerLog() in extensions.ts (~line 4374) fetches …/pods/<pod>/log?tailLines=400 with { headers: { Accept: 'text/plain' } }, and Rancher's cluster proxy answers 406 for that Accept. I put the same request through with an admin bearer token twice: Accept: text/plain -> 406, Accept: */* -> 200 with the pod's real log body.
verdicts.defect: Drop the Accept: text/plain header (or send */*) in devServerLog. The rest of the panel - the ANSI stripping, the line cap, Re-read, Open the terminal - is written and reachable the moment the fetch succeeds.

verdicts.evidence: The card head reads 'Unpublished extensions only ever load on this cluster. A preview is served by the extension's own pod in namespace barn, reached through this cluster's API proxy, so nothing outside this Rancher can load it.' The containment claim matches the mechanism: the preview iframe's src is the in-cluster service proxy (…/api/v1/namespaces/barn/services/http:barn-base-extension:8005/proxy/…).

The matrix head has exactly two column heads: 'CODE REVIEW' carrying <i class="s-icon icon icon-code"> and 'OUTCOME SIGN-OFF' carrying <i class="s-icon icon icon-show">, over two independent three-way controls per destination row - and they really are independent, since on the repository row the code column is locked at Required while the outcome column is settable and persists on its own.
verdicts.defect: The outcome column's glyph is icon-show rather than the design's icon/eye. Same affordance under SIcon's name.

verdicts.evidence: The card head reads 'Everything before the push to a repository is iteration, and Studio never interrupts it. The gate is the moment the extension becomes installable by somebody else.'
The heading reads 'Studio settings' over the scope sentence 'Applies to everyone who uses Studio on this Rancher.'
